article_intent: Establish the definitions used throughout the law: personal data, sensitive personal data, processing, controller, processor, data subject, etc.
implementation_guidance: Build a glossary aligned with PDPL definitions and use it consistently across all privacy artifacts (RoPA, DPIAs, policies, training). Pay attention to the distinction between Controller (decides why and how to process) and Processor (acts on the Controller's behalf) — your contracts and accountabilities depend on which role applies.
evidence_artifacts: Privacy glossary aligned with PDPL definitions; role determination memo per processing activity.

article_intent: Defines when the law applies: any processing of personal data of individuals in KSA, by any controller or processor inside or outside the Kingdom.
implementation_guidance: Run a scope assessment on every business activity that touches personal data of KSA individuals. Extraterritorial reach means foreign Controllers and Processors fall under PDPL when they target or monitor KSA residents. Document your scope determination — it's the foundation of every other PDPL decision.
evidence_artifacts: Scope determination document; activity-by-activity applicability assessment.

article_title: General principles for personal data processing
article_intent: Mandates lawfulness, transparency, purpose limitation, data minimization, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality.
implementation_guidance: These principles are the lens for every processing activity. For each activity in your RoPA, document the lawful basis, declare the purpose, justify the data minimum needed, and define retention. Audit periodically — drift away from these principles is the most common compliance failure.
evidence_artifacts: RoPA showing principles applied; retention schedule; data-minimization review records.

article_intent: Establishes the rights of data subjects: be informed, access, rectification, erasure, withhold consent, complain to the Competent Authority.
implementation_guidance: Build a Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) capability before you need it. Publish how to exercise rights in your privacy notice. Internal SLA for response (PDPL implementing regulations specify 30 days). Train staff to recognize requests in any form (email, social media, web form). Track every request to closure.
evidence_artifacts: DSAR procedure; DSAR form/portal; DSAR response log; staff training records.

article_intent: Data subjects must be informed about the processing of their data: identity of controller, purposes, lawful basis, retention, recipients, rights, transfers.
implementation_guidance: Layered privacy notices: short summary at point of collection, full notice linked. Translate to Arabic and English. Keep notices current — update on every material change to processing. Track which version applied at the time of each consent.
evidence_artifacts: Privacy notices (current and historic); change log; translation evidence.

article_intent: Processing requires consent OR another lawful basis recognized by the law (legal obligation, contract, vital interest, public interest, legitimate interest where balancing favors processing).
implementation_guidance: For every processing activity in the RoPA, identify the lawful basis upfront. Don't default to consent — consent is fragile (can be withdrawn). Where consent is the basis, design withdrawal mechanisms equally easy to use as the original consent process. Document legitimate-interest balancing tests.
evidence_artifacts: RoPA with lawful basis per activity; legitimate interest assessments; consent records.

article_intent: Sensitive data (race, ethnic origin, religion, beliefs, political opinion, health, biometric, genetic, criminal record) requires additional safeguards and explicit consent.
implementation_guidance: Tag sensitive-data processing activities distinctly. Apply enhanced controls: stronger access restrictions, mandatory encryption, narrower retention, explicit and granular consent forms. Consider whether you need to process sensitive data at all — minimization is your friend.
evidence_artifacts: Sensitive data inventory; explicit consent records; enhanced access controls evidence.
gdpr_xref: Article 9 Special categories of personal data

article_intent: Processing of personal data of minors requires consent from a guardian and additional protective measures.
implementation_guidance: If your service is offered to minors or could foreseeably attract them, build age-verification and guardian-consent flows. Default to most-protective settings. Limit profiling. Periodic review for legitimacy of continued processing as the data subject ages.
evidence_artifacts: Age-verification mechanism; guardian-consent records; child-data DPIA.
gdpr_xref: Article 8 Conditions applicable to child's consent

article_intent: Where consent is the basis, it must be freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, and revocable. Bundled consent is invalid.
implementation_guidance: Granular consent — separate purposes get separate toggles. No pre-ticked boxes. Maintain consent records (when, how, what was consented to, what notice version applied). Make withdrawal as easy as granting. Re-confirm consent when material changes occur.
evidence_artifacts: Consent management platform; consent records; withdrawal logs.

article_intent: Direct marketing using personal data requires the data subject's explicit prior consent and an easy opt-out at any time.
implementation_guidance: Opt-in only — no pre-checked boxes. Suppression list managed across all marketing channels (email, SMS, push, calls). Honor opt-out within 24-48 hours across all systems. Document consent provenance for every marketing contact.
evidence_artifacts: Marketing consent records; suppression list; channel-by-channel opt-out test records.

article_intent: Personal data must be accurate and complete. Data subjects may request correction.
implementation_guidance: Self-service rectification portals where feasible. Internal data-quality monitoring. When upstream sources update, propagate changes to all downstream copies. Track rectification requests as part of DSAR workflow.
evidence_artifacts: Data quality monitoring; rectification logs; portal screenshots.

article_intent: Data subjects can request deletion when consent is withdrawn, the purpose is served, or processing is unlawful.
implementation_guidance: Erasure mechanism that propagates to backups, replicas, archives, third-party processors. Some retention requirements (legal, financial, regulatory) may override erasure — document those exceptions. SLA aligned with PDPL response window.
evidence_artifacts: Erasure procedure; cascade-deletion test records; retention-exception register.

article_intent: Where mandated, organizations must appoint a Data Protection Officer with clear independence and authority.
implementation_guidance: Use SDAIA's DPO Appointment Guiding Tool to determine if appointment is mandatory for your activities. If yes, formal appointment letter, reporting line outside privacy-decision making (independence), adequate resources, no conflict of interest. Publish DPO contact in privacy notices. Even when not mandatory, a DPO improves accountability.
evidence_artifacts: DPO appointment letter; DPO job description; DPO independence declaration; reporting-line diagram.

article_intent: DPIAs are required for high-risk processing activities, especially those involving sensitive data or large-scale monitoring.
implementation_guidance: DPIA template embedded in project lifecycle. Trigger criteria: new system handling personal data, automated decisions affecting individuals, sensitive-data processing, surveillance/monitoring, large-scale operations. Engage DPO early. Document residual risks and accept them at appropriate level. Refresh DPIA on material change.
evidence_artifacts: DPIA procedure; completed DPIAs; trigger checklist; sign-off records.

article_intent: Controllers must maintain a Record of Processing Activities documenting all personal data processing.
implementation_guidance: RoPA per activity, not per system. Capture: purpose, lawful basis, data categories, data subject categories, recipient categories, retention period, transfers, security measures. Keep current — refresh on every new processing activity or material change. Make available to SDAIA on request.
evidence_artifacts: RoPA register; quarterly RoPA review records; SDAIA-ready exports.

article_intent: Appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data based on the nature, scope and context of processing.
implementation_guidance: Encryption at rest and in transit. Access controls aligned with least-privilege. Audit logging of personal-data access. Pseudonymization where feasible. Backup and recovery. Vendor-side controls verified. Periodic effectiveness testing. Map controls to NCA ECC where overlap exists for KSA-regulated entities.
evidence_artifacts: Security control inventory; encryption configurations; access reviews; effectiveness test reports.
ndmo_deliverable_ref: Documented Data Security Controls and Countermeasures

article_intent: Notify the Competent Authority and affected data subjects when a breach is likely to result in harm to individuals.
implementation_guidance: Breach response plan with clear triggers, decision tree, communication templates. PDPL Implementing Regulation specifies 72-hour notification window for notifying SDAIA. Notify affected individuals when high risk. Maintain breach register including non-notifiable breaches. Test the response plan annually.
evidence_artifacts: Breach response plan; breach register; breach-drill records; SDAIA notifications archive.

article_intent: Transfer of personal data outside KSA is subject to specific conditions and safeguards. Subject to the separate Cross-Border Transfer Regulation.
implementation_guidance: Map every cross-border data flow. For each, determine the lawful basis under the Cross-Border Transfer Regulation (adequacy decision, binding instruments, standard contractual mechanisms, derogations). Maintain transfer log. Reassess when SDAIA updates the country list or transfer mechanisms.
evidence_artifacts: Cross-border transfer register; transfer mechanism documentation per flow; SCC or equivalent agreements.

article_intent: Processors act only on documented instructions from the Controller. The relationship must be governed by a contract that includes specific safeguards.
implementation_guidance: Standard Data Processing Agreement template covering: subject matter, duration, nature/purpose, types of personal data, categories of data subjects, controller's obligations and rights, processor's specific obligations (confidentiality, sub-processor approval, breach notification, audit rights, return/destruction at end). Embed in every Processor onboarding.
evidence_artifacts: Standard DPA; signed DPAs per Processor; sub-processor register.

article_intent: Specifies the minimum content of privacy notices.
implementation_guidance: Privacy notice checklist: Controller identity and contact, DPO contact (if applicable), purposes, lawful basis, data categories, retention period, recipients, transfers (with safeguards), data subject rights and how to exercise them, complaint right to SDAIA, automated decision-making (if any). Audit annually.
evidence_artifacts: Privacy notice review checklist; content audit reports.

article_intent: Specifies how valid consent must be obtained, recorded, and withdrawn.
implementation_guidance: Granular consent recording with audit trail. Withdrawal mechanism must be as easy as the original grant — same channel, same effort. Re-confirm on material changes. Where children involved, guardian consent verification. Document consent version applicable per data subject.
evidence_artifacts: Consent management platform records; withdrawal audit logs; version-tracking records.

article_intent: Specifies the procedure for responding to data subject requests, including identity verification, scope assessment, and response timeline.
implementation_guidance: DSAR workflow: receipt → identity verification → scope assessment → search/collect → review for exemptions → response. 30-day response window (extendable in complex cases with notice). Standardized response templates. Track all requests including denied or partially-fulfilled with reasons. Internal escalation path.
evidence_artifacts: DSAR procedure document; DSAR register with timestamps; identity verification records; response templates.

article_title: Implementing Regulation: DPIA threshold and content
article_intent: Specifies which processing activities require a DPIA and what the assessment must cover.
implementation_guidance: DPIA mandatory for: processing of sensitive data, large-scale systematic monitoring, automated decisions with legal effects, new technology with privacy implications. DPIA content: description of processing, assessment of necessity and proportionality, identification and assessment of risks, planned measures to mitigate. Senior approval required. Re-assess on material changes.
evidence_artifacts: DPIA procedure with thresholds; completed DPIAs; senior-approval records.

article_intent: Specifies what constitutes a notifiable breach, the 72-hour notification window, content of notifications, and when to notify affected individuals.
implementation_guidance: Breach decision tree: detection → triage → impact assessment → notify SDAIA within 72 hours if criteria met → notify affected individuals if high risk → containment → remediation → lessons learned. Pre-approved notification templates speed response. Include the Implementing Regulation's specified content fields. Internal table-top exercises validate the response.
evidence_artifacts: Breach response plan; pre-approved notification templates; tabletop exercise records; sample notifications.

article_title: Implementing Regulation: DPO appointment criteria and duties
article_intent: Specifies when DPO appointment is mandatory and what duties must be assigned to the DPO.
implementation_guidance: Use SDAIA's DPO Appointment Guiding Tool to assess. If mandatory: formal appointment, independence guaranteed, direct reporting to top management, expertise verified, conflicts of interest avoided, contact published. DPO duties: monitor compliance, advise on DPIAs, point of contact for SDAIA and data subjects, training and awareness.
evidence_artifacts: DPO assessment record (using SDAIA tool); appointment letter; duty statement; reporting line documentation.

article_title: Cross-Border Transfer Regulation: Scope and lawful bases
article_intent: Defines the scope of cross-border transfer rules and the lawful bases under which such transfers may occur.
implementation_guidance: Cross-border transfers must occur under one of the lawful bases (adequacy decision by SDAIA, binding contractual instruments, derogations for specific situations). Most common path: standard contractual clauses approved by SDAIA. Maintain a transfer-register listing every flow with the chosen lawful basis.
evidence_artifacts: Cross-border transfer register; SCC or equivalent contracts; SDAIA adequacy-list snapshots.

article_title: Cross-Border Transfer Regulation: Risk assessment for transfers
article_intent: Mandates a risk assessment for cross-border transfers covering legal, security, and operational risks.
implementation_guidance: Cross-border transfer risk assessment template covering: destination country's data protection regime, government access regimes, security controls of the receiving party, the nature and volume of data, impact of disclosure or unauthorized access. Approve at appropriate level. Refresh annually or when destination country regime changes.
evidence_artifacts: Transfer risk assessment template; completed assessments; refresh records.

article_title: NDMO: Personal data inventory and classification
article_intent: NDMO guidance on building a structured data inventory and classifying data sets by sensitivity for PDPL purposes.
implementation_guidance: Start with a data discovery exercise: catalog every system that processes personal data, the data elements involved, lawful basis, retention period. Classify each data set per the organization's classification scheme aligned with NCA controls (e.g. Public / Internal / Restricted / Critical). Refresh inventory quarterly. Cross-reference to Asset Inventory and RoPA.
evidence_artifacts: Data inventory; classification scheme; quarterly review records.

article_title: NDMO: Privacy by design and default
article_intent: NDMO guidance to embed privacy considerations throughout system design and default settings, before deployment.
implementation_guidance: Privacy review gate in SDLC. New-system DPIA before procurement or build. Default settings most-private (opt-in not opt-out). Data minimization in design. Pseudonymization where feasible. Engage DPO early in design phase. Track every design decision affecting personal data.
evidence_artifacts: SDLC privacy gate procedure; design review minutes; DPIA records linked to projects.
gdpr_xref: Article 25 Data protection by design and by default

article_intent: NDMO guidance on staff awareness and training programs for PDPL compliance.
implementation_guidance: Annual mandatory PDPL training for all staff. Role-based deep training for IT, HR, marketing, customer service. Quarterly refreshers via micro-content. Test understanding via simulations and assessments. Include privacy in onboarding for new joiners. Track completion as a KPI.
evidence_artifacts: Training curriculum; completion records; assessment results; onboarding records.

article_intent: NDMO guidance on continuous compliance monitoring and periodic audits.
implementation_guidance: Compliance monitoring: dashboards tracking RoPA currency, DSAR turnaround time, breach response time, training completion, vendor DPA coverage. Quarterly internal audit of a sample of processing activities. Annual independent audit. Findings tracked to closure with owner and date.
evidence_artifacts: Compliance dashboard; audit programme; audit reports; findings register.
